candidate.name: Hongdae R2 Busking Street
candidate.description: The R2 area, known as the “Street You Want to Walk,” is a pedestrian-friendly street where a wide range of busking performances take place. Performances span multiple genres including pop music, dance, magic, and mime, and are conducted through a prior registration system. During peak tourist seasons in spring and fall, visitors can also enjoy traditional cultural experiences through the “Welcome Event for Tourists.”

candidate.name: Little China Town
candidate.description: Little China Town, the Chinatown in Myeongdong, centers around the Chinese Embassy and has been home to Chinese cuisine restaurants, Chinese elementary schools, and Chinese culture for over 100 years. It is considered the oldest Chinatown in South Korea. The Seoul Overseas Chinese School, located next to the Seoul Central Post Office, has been there since 1909, along with some imported bookstores, Chinese food specialty stores, Chinese product specialty stores, and currency exchange shops. The Hansung Chinese Association handles various tasks such as issuing and processing documents for the Chinese community. This Chinatown developed naturally and is not managed comprehensively. It is one of the places where you can feel an exotic atmosphere in the city.

candidate.name: Jeong-dong Observatory
candidate.description: Jeong-dong Observatory is located on the 13th floor of the Seosomun Building at Seoul City Hall. Inside the observatory, there is a cafe where you can enjoy beverages while taking in a view of the Deoksugung Palace area. Photos depicting the old appearance of Jeongdong are displayed on the cafe walls, allowing visitors to appreciate the historical aspect of the area. There are bar tables by the windows, providing a perfect spot to admire the stunning view while spending time, and there are also group seats, making it ideal for visiting with friends or colleagues. On clear days, you can see Gwanghwamun and the Blue House from the window seats, which are always popular. The cafe at the observatory offers not only coffee but also a variety of drinks like aids and teas at relatively affordable prices, making it a popular spot for many visitors.

candidate.name: Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bukhansan Mountain)
candidate.description: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center is just a 5-minute walk from Exit 2 of Bukhansan Ui Station and offers tourists various hiking services. Focused on Bukhansan Mountain, it provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for different hiking trails in Seoul, including Bugaksan Mountain, Inwangsan Mountain, and Gwanaksan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. In addition to offering themed hiking experience programs for foreigners, the center provides rental services for hiking gear, such as shoes, clothing, trekking poles, gloves, and crampons (available to local visitors accompanying foreigners as well). The center also offers free and paid lockers for convenient storage of belongings. In the lounge, visitors can relax or create lasting memories with friends, family, or companions.

candidate.name: Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bugaksan Mountain)
candidate.description: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bugaksan Mountain) is located on Samcheong-dong Cultural Street and offers a range of services for hiking tourists. Focused on Bugaksan Mountain, it provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for different hiking trails in Seoul, including Bukhansan Mountain, Inwangsan Mountain, and Gwanaksan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. In addition to offering themed hiking experience programs for foreigners, the center provides rental services for hiking gear, such as shoes, clothing, trekking poles, gloves, and crampons (available to local visitors accompanying foreigners as well). The center also offers free and paid lockers for convenient storage of belongings. In the lounge, visitors can relax or create lasting memories with friends, family, or companions.

candidate.name: Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Gwanaksan Mountain)
candidate.description: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Gwanaksan Mountain), located within Gwanaksan Station on the Sillim Line, provides various services for hiking enthusiasts. It focuses on Gwanaksan Mountain and provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for hiking trails in Seoul, including Bukhansan Mountain, Bugaksan Mountain, and Inwangsan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. In addition to offering themed hiking experience programs for foreigners, the center provides rental services for hiking gear, such as shoes, clothing, trekking poles, gloves, and crampons (available to local visitors accompanying foreigners as well). The center also offers lockers for storage upon the use of the gear rental service at no extra cost. In the lounge, visitors can relax or create lasting memories with friends, family, or companions.

candidate.name: YDP CULTURAL LOUNGE DADADA
candidate.description: Located in the plaza of Yeongdeungpo Times Square, "DADADA" is a lively cultural lounge that serves as a dynamic hub for residents and visitors. Offering various cultural events and programs, it captures the playful spirit of children who once filled the neighborhood with cheerful trumpet sounds. "DADADA" aims to infuse Yeongdeungpo with vitality by sharing diverse voices and stories. The space hosts everything from exhibitions and workshops to immersive media art experiences, positioning itself as a hub for art and creative expression. Through collaborations with local artists and the community, it organizes engaging events in a modern, thoughtfully designed space that also invites relaxation. With its welcoming atmosphere, "DADADA" provides a place where people of all ages can connect, communicate, and participate in rich cultural exchanges.

candidate.name: Seongsu Pedestrian Overpass
candidate.description: Seongsu-dong offers fantastic spots to take in Seoul’s breathtaking sunsets and night views. As the golden hour nears, photography enthusiasts gather with their cameras in hand. You can capture iconic landmarks from the bridge, such as the Hangang River, Namsan Tower, Seongsudaegyo Bridge, Seongdong-gu, and even Hannam-dong in Yongsan-gu. On the opposite side of the Namsan view, Lotte World Tower glows in soft pink hues. If you head down below the pedestrian bridge, you’ll find Hangang River Park, a perfect spot to relax while watching the sunset reflect off the river. Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes before sunset to catch the best sunset views.

candidate.name: Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education Namsan Library
candidate.description: Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library, originally opened in 1922 as the Gyeongseong Municipal Library in Myeong-dong. Situated in the heart of Namsan, the current building was constructed in 1965 following a public design competition. It has since been recognized as a Seoul Future Heritage building. The library boasts a collection of invaluable resources, including three volumes designated as Seoul City Tangible Cultural Properties and 227 volumes of 30 registered cultural properties. With a collection of around 500,000 books, 16,000 non-book materials, and 800 serial publications, Namsan Public Library is committed to preserving and sharing knowledge. In collaboration with the National Library of Korea, it has created a digital archive of rare and valuable materials, including ancient books and East Asian texts. Additionally, the library serves as a specialized resource center for Seoul's residents, offering various programs designed to enrich their cultural and intellectual lives.

candidate.name: Myeongdong Jaemi-ro
candidate.description: Jaemi-ro is a comic street located in Myeongdong, Jung-gu. It is a content-specialized street within Sangsang Town's cultural content clustering, centered around the former Seoul Animation Center (currently undergoing reconstruction). It's a themed street stretching approximately 450m from Exit 3 of Myeongdong Station to the former Seoul Animation Center, adorned with Korean comics, animations, characters, illustrations, and other content. Jaemi-ro, connecting the iconic tourist spots of Seoul, Myeongdong, and Namsan Mountain, offers a valuable experience where visitors can enjoy diverse cultural experiences within the heart of Seoul's downtown area.

candidate.name: Changsin-Sungin Quarry Observatory
candidate.description: The quarry observatory is built atop the summit of Changsin-dong quarry, providing a panoramic view of the city and natural landscapes at a glance. During the Japanese colonial period, a quarry was located in Naksan, Changsin-dong, to supply stone for the exterior of large buildings such as the Government-General of Korea, the old Seoul Station, and the Bank of Korea. After the Korean War, the quarry's use was discontinued, but the quarry observatory was located where immigrants and refugees settled to form a village. From the quarry observatory, with nothing obstructing the view, you can enjoy the skyline of Seoul at a glance. The second floor houses a coffee shop (Café Nakta), and the third floor features an outdoor observation deck, allowing you to appreciate the scenery of Seoul's cityscape and nature from any vantage point. Especially renowned is the breathtaking view that unfolds alongside the sunset. Enjoy the best panoramic view, a reasonably priced cup of coffee, and homemade ggangjeong and Nakta rice cakes. Small music concerts featuring historical and cultural stories, exhibitions, and live guitar performances are held occasionally.

candidate.name: Changsin-dong's Cliff Village
candidate.description: Changsin-dong Cliff Village, located in Changsin 1, 2, and 3-dong in Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, has undergone various transformations over the years. It was a quarry village in the 1960s, a wooden village in the 1970s, a sewing factory in the 1990s, and finally a sewing village in the 2000s. It is situated around the rocky cliffs once used as the nation's only quarry. Changsin-dong Cliff Village is divided into densely packed, dilapidated, aged homes built on cliffs and precipices and homes formed beneath rocky hills. *Please Note: When visiting, please refrain from making excessive noise, as actual residents live there.

candidate.name: Ihwa Mural Village
candidate.description: Below Naksan Fortress, Ihwa-dong, once a quiet neighborhood, transformed into a mural village after the 'Naksan Project.' With murals painted throughout the alleyways, have fun searching for them as you explore the village. As you climb the stairs, don't forget to turn around and enjoy the panoramic view of Seoul.

candidate.name: Bulgwang Blacksmith Workshop
candidate.description: This blacksmith shop is run by two generations, father and son, and the first owner, Mr. Park Kyung-won, has been a blacksmith for over 60 years. His son, Park Sang-bum, has been a blacksmith for 26 years, and they work together to keep Bulgwang Blacksmith Shop running. All the tools made at Bulgwang Blacksmith Shop are handmade and differentiated from those made in factories. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

candidate.name: LCDC SEOUL
candidate.description: LCDC SEOUL was built where anauto repair shop and a shoe manufacturing factory once existed. A building wasadded to the existing two factory buildings to recreate the space into a culturecomplex. It's hard to find any traces of the old auto shop, but the dark grayconcrete walls wrapping around LCDC SEOUL still blend seamlessly into thesurrounding industrial landscape. You start the morning with asweet dessert and cup of tea in the first floor cafe, move up to the second andthird floor for different cultural experiences, and reach the bar on the fourthfloor around sundown for a drink. There is no need to move to another locationsince there is plenty to do all day in this truly cultural space.

candidate.name: Yangcheon Park Book Shelter
candidate.description: At one side of Yangcheon Park, where an energy of people doing exercise and freeness of people enjoying a walk are in harmony, has a space to enjoy reading mingling with the nature. Yangcheon Park Book Shelter with a shape of a windmill that the three curved lines towards insidestand back to back and surround by putting the cylinder bookshelf as a pivot, is a space wherethe beauty of curves is emphasized. Along the curved lines, which seems like they’re embracingthe park, they’ve made large windows, so it’s possible to bodily enjoy the nature of the park insidethe library.

candidate.name: NaeSup Library
candidate.description: ‘NaeSup Library’, which has opened to commemorate the 100 th anniversary of a poet, Yun Dong-ju’s birth brought the name from the front phrase of his poem, ‘A new path’. The library, locatedbetween the residential area where the multi-household houses are crowded and an azure park, isconnecting the town and the park as the verse of the poem, ‘beyond the hill, into the village’. The library appearance of inverted trapezoid has a green exterior as the forest beyond the library. Stair-type bookshelf, created along the steep slope of an apperance is the characteristic of 'NaeSup Library'.

candidate.name: Gyeongui Line Book Street
candidate.description: Gyeongui Line Book Street is a well-known cultural hub with a book theme at Hongdae Station along the Gyeongui Line. It is also a place where you can participate in various programs such as themed walk & talks related to books every month. You can even meet different authors and talk to them. Many people enjoy the warm sunshine and take a leisurely stroll through Gyeongui Line Book Street.

candidate.name: Malli-dong
candidate.description: The Malli-dong neighborhood, located near Seoul Station, has been gaining popularity ever since the opening of Seoullo 7071, a sky garden and pedestrian road. This historic district of Seoul is home to a variety of restaurants with delectable food and trendy coffee shops. This area dates back to the state of Joseon, so the locals associate it with the history of the city.

candidate.name: Eunpyeong Hanok Village
candidate.description: Located in Jingwan-dong of Eunpyeong-gu, the Eunpyeong Hanok Village captures a quaint, serene landscape with the Bukhansan Mountain serving as the backdrop for the modern, neatly-built hanoks. The village is set in greater Seoul in the vicinity of Yeonsinnae and Ilsan. If you take a snapshot from the middle of the road between the tall hanok structures, it'll give you the feeling of standing on the set of some historical film set during the Joseon Dynasty. There are also plenty of sites to see if you walk up from the hanok village along the deck path that will lead you to the Jingwansa Temple, Literature Museum, and more!

candidate.name: Seocho Tourist Information Center
candidate.description: Making Memories at Seocho Tourist Information Center Venue: Between Exits 9 and 10 of Gangnam Station Target Audience: Open to everyone (Korean nationals & foreigners) Programming: VR tour, chromakey photo zone, hanbok and Korean instruments hands-on programs, letter-sending, etc. Fee: Free admissions

candidate.name: Daerim Market & Gamjaguk Street
candidate.description: Gamjaguk is a must-eat dish for those visiting Eungam-dong! With restaurants inside Daerim Market selling gamjaguk made by boiling pork ribs, potatoes, and cabbage since mid-1980s, the area became popularized as Gamjaguk Street. With competition getting fierce, restaurants started to experiment and develop their own unique broth recipes, eventually leading to more and more people knowing about Eungam-dong's gamjaguk.

candidate.name: Seorae Village
candidate.description: Seorae Village is named for the " seoriseori," or winding and twisting streams that once flowed next to the village. Today, the area is better known for the multitude of French restaurants, cafes, wine bars, and trendy stores that thrive here. There is also a thriving community of French expats here, and of the 1,000 or so French nationals in Korea, half of them reside in Seorae Village. The village is located close to the Gangnam neighborhood.

candidate.name: Insadong
candidate.description: Nowhere exudes more local and traditional charm than Insa-dong, a quaint neighborhood in the center of Seoul that transports visitors back to a time when women wore hanbok and men rode horses. With its wooden tea houses, boutique galleries and street vendors selling traditional snacks, a stroll through Insa-dong is mandatory for all visitors, especially on Sundays when the streets become traffic free and come alive with street performances, buskers and throngs of young and old who have come to experience one of Seoul’s most fascinating and creative neighborhoods. While the entertainment here is free, Insa-dong is also one of the best places in Seoul to purchase traditional Korean art, products, and other souvenirs, as it is filled with antique shops, art galleries, traditional stationery shops, handicraft shops, pottery and porcelain shops, bookstores, and art supply stores. Insa-dong is also home to many traditional restaurants and tea houses. Frequently Asked Questions about Insadong-gil Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting near Insadong-gil? These are the following tourist attractions around Insadong-gil. • Ssamzie-gil • Nagwon Instrument Arcade • Cheonggyecheon Stre

candidate.name: Hongdae
candidate.description: Hongdae is the scene where Korean culture, both pop and indie, manifests, especially at night. More information on planning a Sangam day trip can be soon found at K-stars and their K-style if the Korean Wave has washed over you, then there’s no better place to tread the path of such tastemakers as Hongdae, the live-wire district of music and art culture. Whether you’ve come on your own or with equally eager friends, the ever-trending university area remains the only place in Seoul where you can transitionfrom daytime exploring to nighttime adventures just as easily as you shuffle through your K-Pop playlist. Shopping in Hongdae Across the street and around the corner is a three-story store aptly named Around the Corner, Its multi-designer displays only cover two floors, but the smaller selection gives customers room to consider the subtler hip-hop motifs and mixed prints that punctuate the street wear-filled racks. Remember, just because Hongdae is more casual and “free” than, say, Gangnam or Apgujeong, doesn’t mean fashion doesn’t matter. The vibe you can see from the stores and the people on the streets, is effortless withan edge of the true Hongdae touch. You can see more of tha

candidate.name: Itaewon
candidate.description: Korea is one of the most ethnically homogeneous countries in the world, but you'd never know that walking down the streets of Itaewon. Located smack-dab in the center of Seoul, Itaewon is home for the majority of expats that reside in Korea, making Itaewon a mini melting pot of cultures and religions from all over the world. The Seoul Central Mosque is also located in Itaewon along with a number of halal food stores, and large numbers of US military personnel can be seen here as the Yongsan Garrison that is stationed nearby. Due to the area’s diverse inhabitants, Itaewon has become one of the most cosmopolitan areas in Seoul boasting restaurants, shopping and nightlife that are equally diverse and cater to international tastes, attracting many other foreigners and tourists. It is safe to say that Itaewon is almost better known by foreigners and non-Korean residents than Koreans. Itaewon is known as the place to go when you want to get your foreign food fix. Restaurants featuring cuisine from all over the world can be found here including Indian, Thai, Pakistani, Greek, German, French, Italian, Australian, English, American, and Mexican, cuisines which are not easily found in Korea.

candidate.name: Daehak-ro
candidate.description: Daehak-ro (sometimes spelled Daehangno) is Seoul's theater and performing arts district. Daehak-ro is the name of the neighborhood and the area's main road. Daehak-ro Street stretches from Jongno 4ga to Hyehwa Rotary. There are numerous theaters and performance venues of all sizes located throughout the area. Visitors who are fans of theater, musicals, and music should head to Daehak-ro to get their fill of cultural experiences.

candidate.name: Seoul Music
candidate.description: Opened in 1972, Seoul Music continues to exist in the underground shopping center below City Hall. A witness to the explosive growth of Korea's music market, this store has remained standing, taking in and remembering all the ups and down of history.

candidate.name: Nature Poem
candidate.description: Nature Poem is a six-story commercial gallery located in the heart of Gangnam's posh Cheongdam-dong neighborhood. Cheongdam-dong is famous for its abundance of premium designer stores. Nature Poem is located near many art galleries and high-end luxury stores, making a visit to Nature Poem a convenient starting point for a tour of Gangnam. Gallery GO, the Nam June Paik Museum and Gallery Jang are all nearby.

candidate.name: Seo Gallery
candidate.description: The Seo Gallery is an arts gallery in Banpo-dong, Seoul. Its exhibitions cover a wide variety of different mediums including, but not limited to, painting, sculpture, photography, architecture, design, and fashion. The gallery also provides various programs to support both older artists and to foster new artists.

candidate.name: Mullae Art Village
candidate.description: The Mullae Art Village is an area that was once known for its steel foundries but has transformed into an artists' village in recent years. There are numerous artists' studios and workshops here as well as great cafes and restaurants. Nearly every corner of the area is adorned with colorful murals and outdoor sculptures. There is much to see and photograph here. On weekends, most studios and workshops close so visitors will get a rare chance to see artwork that adorns window shutters and doors.
reviews: Seoul City Tour Bus is the easiest way to see most of the place of interest in Seoul.You get on & off from the bus at the designated stops, and see Gyeongbokgung Palace, National Folk Museum, N Seoul Tower, and Namsangol Hanok Village etc. Get down in time & watch the changing of the guards during a stop at Gwanghwamun Gate.

candidate.name: TETEROTSALON
candidate.description: TETEROTSALON, one of the well-known K-fashion brands, is located on Hanok Street in Ikseon-dong, a hot place in Seoul It has a high quality as a brand where designers based on the traditional Korean design style gather to produce their own clothes. It sells various unique gift products from Korea and clothing, so it is a good place to shop for gifts and souvenirs. If you are looking for unique Korean gifts during a tour, please visit.
reviews: TETEROT Salon was one of my favorite shopping discoveries in Seoul. The boutique is set inside a beautifully restored hanok, blending traditional Korean architecture with modern fashion. The interior alone is worth a visit—the cherry blossom installations, warm wood beams, and thoughtfully designed displays make it feel more like a gallery than a clothing store. Their clothing is a modern interpretation of hanbok and Korean fashion. The pieces are feminine, elegant, and wearable in everyday life. I especially loved the wrap skirts and flowing silhouettes that incorporate traditional Korean elements without looking like costumes. The staff gave me space to browse without pressure, and the fitting rooms made it easy to try things on. The quality of the fabrics and construction felt noticeably higher than many of the tourist-oriented shops nearby. Even if you don’t buy anything, I highly recommend stopping in for inspiration and photos. If you’re looking for a unique piece of Korean fashion instead of another souvenir, this is one of the best boutiques in Ikseon-dong. Highlights: * Beautiful hanok boutique * Elegant modern hanbok-inspired clothing * High-quality fabrics and craftsmanship * Peaceful shopping atmosphere * A must-visit for anyone who appreciates Korean design and fashion

candidate.name: Gaemi Supermarket
candidate.description: Opened in the 1900s, Gaemi Super has a history with the surrounding sewing industry. There were many sewing shops leading from Seoul Station to Namdaemun Market. The employees of the sewing shops were the customers of the store, but in the 2000s, the sewing industry became specialized and the store's sales plummeted. However, in 2015, foreigners started coming to the area, and they started taking pictures with them, and it became a culture. As a testament to this, one wall of Gaemi Super is covered with photos of foreign customers and the owner.

candidate.name: Chunchusa
candidate.description: Chunchusa is a 60-year-old gown shop that has been in business for three generations. Numerous degree gowns in a variety of materials and colors fill one side of the store, and a separate room is dedicated to ironing the gowns. Chunchusa has been specializing in degree gowns since 1960. In a year, the company rents out about 60,000 gowns. Chunchusa enjoys making clothes that commemorate someone's special moment, and this joy is reflected in work.

candidate.name: Yeonhee Photo Studio
candidate.description: Founded in the 1950s, Yeonhee Photo Studio has been in operation for over 65 years with three generations of owners. Offering high-quality photos and quick retouching services, Yeonhee Photo Studio is popular with both Korean and foreign customers. There is a powder room where you can apply makeup and do your hair before your photo shoot, and they have a wide selection of headbands and hair accessories. Yeonhee Photo Studio is considered to be a popular spot for "employment photos," and it is said that having your job application photo taken here increases your chances of getting hired.

candidate.name: Haechang Tailor Shop
candidate.description: Haechang Tailor shop is Sogong-dong’s oldest tailor shop with over 90 years of history. Having started its origin in Bosu-dong, Busan back in 1929, it moved locations to Sogong-dong, Seoul in 1945 and developed an impressive list of clientele including many historical figures in Korea. Haechang Tailor Shop was a beloved shop of many prominent political figures in Korean history. This shop was able continue to maintain business due to their high quality service and suits. Through constant communication with their customers, the shop make suits that accurately reflect the individual customer's style through details. One of Korea's first tailor shop, many students who used to learn and work in this store has set up their own tailor shops throughout Korea.

candidate.name: Yuil Oriental Medicine Clinic
candidate.description: Yuil Oriental Medicine Clinic was founded in 1945 by Dr. Lee Taek-sung, the father of the current president, and has remained in the same location ever since. The Jongno-gu area was originally densely populated with oriental medicine clinics and herbal medicine shops, and at one point there were 300 of them. Today, the number of clinics has decreased, but the only cli nic still stands. It is the 'only' oriental medicine clinic, as the name suggests, that has been practicing the old acupuncture methods that are different from other clinics. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

candidate.name: Dol Record
candidate.description: Since 1975, Dole Records has been selling LP, CD, and cassette tapes that contain someone's memories. Word of mouth has spread like wildfire about this treasure trove, and it continues to attract record lovers to this day. It is one of the few remaining record stores in Seoul that not only retains its original appearance, but also has a large selection of LPs, cassette tapes, and CDs that symbolize Korean popular music from the 70s to the 90s.

candidate.name: Daegu Sesame Oil
candidate.description: When walking along Gyedong-gil in Bukchon, there is a place that stops you in your tracks with its savory sesame oil smell. The owner, who has more than 40 years of oil experience, squeezes and sells the oil himself, and has been running a sesame oil shop in the same place since 1975. There are many regular customers, but foreign tourists often come here to buy sesame oil after seeing it in magazines or on TV. They sell sesame and perilla oils that are no more than a week old, so you can be sure of their freshness. They also deliver nationwide.

candidate.name: Munhwa Barber Shop
candidate.description: Munhwa Barber Shop has been around for 78 years. Both the exterior and interior appearance of this shop has remained unchanged over the years, leading to an atmospheric shop which leads visitors to reminisce about the past.

candidate.name: Tongmungwan
candidate.description: Tongmungwan is an old bookstore that opened in 1934, and has been opening for three generations. It is a bookstore that discovers, evaluates, analyzes, distributes, and publishes ancient Korean books, and has discovered numerous cultural assets such as "Wolin Seokbo" and "Independent Newspaper." It is currently run by Lee Jong-un, the grandson of founder and first director Lee Geom-ro. The main customers are those who study and study ancient books, collectors who invest in the value of ancient books, and Japanese and Chinese tourists who are familiar with Chinese characters, according to the commission. • This place has been selected as a ' Seoul Future Heritage '. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.

candidate.name: Napcheong Bronzeware
candidate.description: Napcheongnotjeon is a brassware shop that continues the organic production method of the Napcheong region of North Pyongan Province. It has been selling Bangja organic brassware in Insadong since 1986 and has been practicing the method for more than half a century, making it a favorite among locals and foreigners alike. Most of the products are made by Lee Bong-joo, who was the first person in Korea to be designated as an Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 77 in 1983, and his eldest son, Lee Hyung-geun, who took over the business in 2015.
reviews: The best quality of Korean bronze tableware, at the best price, with a large panel of choices.

candidate.name: Gukseon Otchil
candidate.description: This store has been selling lacquerware since 1977. The store has a history of 40 years and is run by two generations. The first-generation owner came to Seoul alone when he was 19 years old and learned the craft for the first time at a lacquer workshop that solves room and board. Located in Gwangjang Market, the project was acquired by his son, a cultural asset function, under the new name of national lacquer. Today, the business exports mother-of-pearl products to countries around the world and has developed its reputation as a traditional craft shop representing Korean style. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. candidate.description: Pungwoldang is a classical music store and cultural space in Cheongdam-dong. Visitors can shop for classical music CDs and books on classical music. There is even a listening room dubbed "Pungwolchae." Pungwoldang hosts cultural events such as lectures on classical music, video screenings, and musical events. Pungwoldang also has a cafe that sells light refreshments.

candidate.name: Hongdae Free Market
candidate.description: Hongdae (Hongik University) Free Market is a marketplace for young artists. The market is run in a flea market format, but while a typical flea market sells second-hand goods, the Free Market sells only genuinely creative artwork. Since 2002, the market has been held every Saturday and has since become the prime cultural hotspot on Hongdae street, and a venue for performances by indie bands and different cultural events. The Free Market also introduces organizations who work for public good, hosts tours and workshops, and hosts the Afternoon Stage for local artists and musicians to perform at.

candidate.name: Kwanchenru Street: The Little Chinese Quarter of Seoul
candidate.description: Kwanchenru Street is an unofficial cultural district located in Myeong-dong that is home to incredible Chinese restaurants and stores. Kwanchenru is the Chinese pronunciation of the Korean word "gwancheonga", which means the street in front of a government office. At one of end of Kwanchenru is the Chinese Embassy. Authentic, delicious Chinese food can be had here and there are several famous restaurants here such as Din Tai Fung. There are also several shops selling Chinese antiques, souvenirs, and books. Kwanchenru Street is a well-kept secret for some of the best Chinese restaurants in Seoul.

candidate.name: Songridan-gil
candidate.description: Let's relax at the atmospheric terrace cafe with the beautiful Seokchon Lake. Lotte World, Lotte Tower, and nearby apartments offer stunning views at night.

candidate.name: Gyeongnidan-gil
candidate.description: Although it is part of Itaewon-dong, it is a famous street because of its different atmosphere from Itaewon! It is a cultural and youthful space famous for its diverse and unique food, and there are more bars and cafes with good atmospheres than regular restaurants, so it is a place that many foreigners staying in Korea visit.

candidate.name: Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Center
candidate.description: Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall, built as a residential and commercial building in the 1960s, appeared as "Geumga Plaza" in the drama Vincenzo and has become a hot place to visit ever since. This shopping mall is considered to be the first electronics shopping center in Korea. Its name "Sewoon" means "a place that collects the energy of the world." Nowadays, visitors can find the popular cafes of the Euljiro district here, such as Horangi Cafe. Additionally, from the rooftop of the Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall, visitors can see the fantastic night views of Namsan Tower, Cheonggyecheon Stream, and the Jongno district. Visit Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall and the popular cafes in the Euljiro district as you recall scenes from your favorite TV series.

candidate.name: Cheongdamdong Fashion Street
candidate.description: Cheongdam currently boasts the world's major luxury brands lined up neatly for your shopping pleasure. Present are renowned brands such as Louis Vuitton, Prada, Cartier, and Burberry, but also avant-garde international and Korean designers such as Martin Margiela and Son Jung Wan. The boutiques installed here are all about providing clients with lifestyle experiences that would have you come back and spend lots more of your money -- Seoul’s luxury experience is all about excellent service and hospitality. Many of the shops also operate their own restaurants and cafes inside, and regularly launch exclusive promotions and events in an effort to close the distance between the brands and the consumers. Cheongdam is also known for its cluster of beauty and hair salons with floors and floors of beauty experts offering complete "Seoulite" makeovers, nails, face or body massages, hairdos.This is where Korean celebrities come to get their makeup done (as well as re-model their body parts - have we mentioned that Seoul is also the mecca of plastic surgery?), which is why Cheongdam is also called "Celebrity Street".

candidate.name: Geumcheon Course
candidate.description: The Geumcheon-gu area is a great place to find IT products, cultural items, activities, good food, and more due to the cluster of big shopping malls. Mario Outlet carries famous brands and good quality items, but always seeks to offer the biggest discount possible 365 days a year. W Mall is a leading fashion outlet that carries women's clothing, men's clothing, casual wear, fashion accessories, sportswear, outdoor wear, and children's clothing. 300 well-known Korean brands are gathered at this one place and offered to customers at a reasonable price. At the Hyundai outlet in Gasan, you have access to famous brands for up to 80% off all year long. As part of a way to establish more creative spaces in the Seoul, the Seoul Art Space was created by remodeling a printing plant in October 2009. This space is intended to encourage and help artists step into their gifts, while also allowing the public to enjoy art and culture through a variety of programs.

candidate.name: Garosu-gil Road
candidate.description: Garosu-gil has quickly became one of Seoul's hottest neighborhoods in recent years. 20 years ago, this place was once a densely populated area filled with galleries and packed with designer shops. At one point, many film companies spotted the area, and at other times, various artists set up shop here. So there plenty of neat, older shops in the Garosu-gil area. Additionally, there are many fashion stores that have become quite popular. The stores in the area are diverse, from antique furniture stores to bookstores selling foreign books. It is also a good walking area. It's also very easy for visitors to come across their new favorite cafes while strolling around the neighborhood. In addition to clothing stores, visitors can find plenty of exhibitions and galleries to check out. Frequently Asked Questions about Garosu-gil What is the nearest subway station to Garosu-gil? The closest subway stations to Garosu-gil are Sinsa Station (Sinbundang Line, Subway Line 3 - Exit 8) and Apgujeong Station (Subway Line 3 - Exit 4). Where is the closest Hangang Park to Garosu-gil? The nearest Hangang Park to Garosu-gil is Jamwon Hangang Park .

candidate.name: Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street
candidate.description: Located at subway line 8 Munjeong station, Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street is considered to be Korea's first outlet shopping district. The street began when shops selling off excess clothing stock opened here one by one. After walking about 500 meters from exit 1 of Munjeong Station, a cowboy statue first welcomes visitors. From here, the 2.5 kilometers of Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street begin, also known as the first fashion avenue. Both sides of the street are full with over 200 brand-name shops, making it easy to browse several famous brands at once. Always popular with shoppers are the 100 individual shops, as well as the multi-fashion malls such as Modes, Dump etc. or the outlet shops such as Cheil Industries Inc. and LG Fashion. When you start to feel tired from shopping, Zelkova Park, situated just behind Munjeong-dong Office is the perfect place to take a rest. The park has a 600-year-old zelkova tree and provides refreshing rest areas. There are many restaurants, cafes, amusement arcades, food courts etc. located nearby, providing lots of interesting things to see, do and eat. As the nation's oldest outlet street, various festivals and cultural events are frequently held on Munjeong

candidate.name: Mokdong Rodeo Street
candidate.description: Mokdong Rodeo Street features fashion outlets which offer a wide range of well-known brands at discounted prices throughout the year. The street is easily accessible as it is situated close to Mokdong Station, Subway Line 5. Since it was formed in 1994, the reputation of Mokdong Rodeo Street has as a fashion and cultural district has steadily grown. It is also a popular shopping destination for overseas tourists as they can purchase high-quality brands at discounted prices. Situated in the middle of Mokdong apartment complex, Mokdong Rodeo Street is the originator of outlet stores, but has many features that are different from other outlets. First of all, clothing stores are grouped together by category into themed streets, for example, ladies’, men’s, casual and golf wear, rather than being scattered individually. Furthermore, as most stores are located on ground level, it is the perfect place for window-shopping as you take a stroll. Everything about Rodeo Street has been designed with the shoppers’ convenience in mind.

candidate.name: Yongsan Mill
candidate.description: Running its business near Ichon-dong's railroad for the past 30 years, Yongsan Mill was created by an owner who used to work in a rice cake factory. Able to make any kind of rice cake using high quality ingredients, Yongsan Mill has become a beloved place for many of its local residents. Not only do they make rice cake, but they also makes sesame oil and crushes red pepper flakes like any other regular mill.

candidate.name: Sewoon Shopping Center
candidate.category: History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
candidate.description: The Sewoon Shopping Center was founded in 1968 as Korea's first electronics market under the mission of creating a thriving business community complex and has been around for over 40 years. The center reached its height during the 1970s & 80s as Korea's "go-to" electronics market but has also experienced a few low points along the way. However, in 2017, the Dasi Sewoon Project advocated for the second rise of the market as a "Maker City" that embraces both the creative manufacturing and creative printing industries. The market offers not only a wide selection of electronics and electrical products such as appliances, parts, audio devices, security cameras, arcade games, karaoke equipment and lighting equipment, but it is also home to a variety of other sites and attractions, such as the Sewoon Rooftop where Seoul's past and present converge into a single panoramic view, the sky-deck walkway, which is open to the public and crosses the Cheonggyecheon Stream, Sewoon Hall, a culture complex celebrating Joseon Dynasty cultural values, and the Cheonggye Sanghoe, a market filled with items specific to different regions and communities throughout the country.

candidate.name: Itaewon Global Village Festival
candidate.description: From October 17-18, the "2015 Itaewon Global Village Festival" will take place in Itaewon, an area that is considered to be a special tourist zone. The festival will be one dynamic event. The highlight is definitely the global village parade, then there is the fashion show with traditional clothing, a "DJ festival" that has the unconditional support of the younger generation, a chance to see the culture of different countries, and also a chance to try foods from different nations as well. For the first time this year, the audience will be able to participate in quizzes, a traditional form of tug-of-war, a Korean game of popping a plastic balloon-like structure, and other events that are tailored for a large sum of people so that everyone can join in at once. The main stage will be at Noksapyeong station, but there will be separate smaller stages all around the Itaewon area and Bogwang-ro, where you can see traditional folk performances, participate in the global village quiz, see street performances, and various other forms of entertainment.

candidate.name: Gwanghwamun International Art Festival
candidate.description: The Gwanghwamun International Art Festival (GIAF) is an annual art festival that aims to improve the quality of Korean art and pop culture. The festival takes place from May 29 - June 24 at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts and The Story of King Sejong Exhibition Hall located in Gwanghwamun Square. The work of more than 500 domestic and international artists will be exhibited for people to enjoy. In addition to viewing the art exhibits, visitors will also be able to enjoy various performances and try different kinds of arts and crafts including ceramics, color therapy, silver handicrafts, leather handicrafts and more.

candidate.name: Music at the Royal Palace
candidate.description: Starting from May 4 until October 13, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ will be held at Changdeokgung (Palace), Deoksugung (Palace), Gyeongbokgung (Palace) and Jongmyo (Royal Shrine). After the first successful traditional arts performance in 2008, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ has become a permanant show since 2009. Every spring and autumn, each palace offers a wealth of cultural events to watch for both locals and foreigners who visit. ｢Music at the Royal Palace｣ not only provides entertainment for vistors with traditional musical performances and storytelling, but also offers visitors a chance to experience the elegance of palaces and the depth of traditional Korean arts by bringing culture, history and arts together. In order for viewers to truly experience the beauty and original atmosphere of the palace and music, the stage, sounds and lightings have all been reduced to a minimum. Experience the elegance of Court Music ｢Changdeokgung (Palace) Concert｣ Changdeokgung (Palace), designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, will be holding a very special concert. candidate.name: Seoul International Fireworks Festival
candidate.description: ※ The 2016 Schedule Is Coming Soon The Seoul International Fireworks Festival is held in early October of each year in front of the 63 City Building at Yeouido Hangang Park. This festival is one of Seoul's most popular fall events, and watching fireworks paint the sky and water in a breathtaking spectacle. The massive crowds that gather around the Hangang River also adds to the festive atmosphere. For the best views, head over to Yeouinaru Station and walk along the river until 63 City Building. If crowds make you uncomfortable, go to the following locations to enjoy the fireworks in relative peace and quiet: Ichon Hangang Park, Nodeul Island, Hangang Bridge Observatory, Sayukshin Park, Seonyudo Park, and Noryangjin Seafood Market Parking Tower. 2015 Schedule and Program 13:00~19:00: Public participation programs (Stage performances, etc.) 19:00~19:20: Opening Ceremony 19:20~19:35: U.S.A fireworks display 19:40~19:55: Phillipines fireworks display 20:00~20:40: Korea fireworks display 20:40~21:30: DJ performances (D zone) / Public participation "clean campaign"
